items.stem: Inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Which concept is applied?
items.answer: Prudence

items.stem: Explain the prudence concept, using an example.
items.answer: Profits and assets are not overstated, liabilities and losses not understated, e.g. inventory at lower of cost and NRV, allowance for doubtful debts.
items.markingKey: Meaning [1]; example [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the consistency concept is important to users of financial statements.
items.answer: If the same methods are used each year, changes in profit reflect real performance rather than changes in accounting policy, so results can be compared over time.
items.markingKey: Comparison over time [1]; changes reflect performance not method [1] [2]

items.answer: Consistency.

(a) Identify the accounting concept applied in each situation. (b) Explain why it is appropriate to apply this concept in situation (i).
items.answer: (a) (i) going concern; (ii) consistency; (iii) prudence; (iv) relevance (b) Applying going concern gives users a true and fair view: the business is assumed to continue trading for the foreseeable future, so assets are valued at cost less depreciation, not at break-up value.

items.stem: Explain how the going concern concept affects the valuation of non-current assets.
items.answer: Because the business is expected to continue, assets are valued at cost less depreciation over their useful lives, not at the lower amount they would fetch in a forced sale.
items.markingKey: Continue trading assumed [1]; cost less depreciation not break-up value [1] [2]

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) Jonas has always used the straight-line method to depreciate equipment and does not switch to the reducing-balance method this year, even though it would increase profit by $32,800 (ii) The auditors of Pacific Tiles were concerned that a major customer owing $1,500 had collapsed and that the business might have to close; they questioned whether assets should be valued at break-up values. An accounts assistant stated that situation (i) is an example of the substance over form concept. Explain the error and calculate the correct concept, showing your working.
items.answer: The situation shows consistency: once a method is chosen it should be used from year to year so that results can be compared; substance over form means transactions are recorded according to their economic reality rather than their legal form. Correct concept: consistency.

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) Pampas Leather values its machinery at cost less depreciation of $25,100 rather than at the $42,000 it would fetch if sold today (ii) Nadia creates an allowance for doubtful debts of $15,900 because some customers are paying late, but does not record an expected gain of $21,200 from a lawsuit (iii) Orchid Pharmacy uses a delivery van under a five-year lease and records it as a non-current asset, although it does not legally own the van. A student stated that situation (i) is an example of the duality concept. Explain the error and calculate the correct concept, showing your working.
items.answer: The situation shows going concern: the business is assumed to continue trading for the foreseeable future, so assets are valued at cost less depreciation, not at break-up value; duality means every transaction has two aspects, recorded by a debit and a credit of equal value. Correct concept: going concern.

items.stem: Explain the business entity concept and why it is applied even to a sole trader.
items.answer: The business is treated as separate from its owner so only business transactions are recorded; this shows the true performance and position of the business, even though the law does not separate a sole trader from the business.

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of the historical cost concept.

items.answer: Materiality depends on size relative to the business: $5,000 may affect decisions about a small shop but be insignificant for a large company.

items.answer: Revenue is recognised when the goods or services have passed to the customer and the customer has accepted liability to pay, not when the cash is received.

items.answer: (a) (i) comparability; (ii) faithful representation; (iii) materiality (b) Applying comparability may reduce reported profit or take extra work, but it gives users reliable, comparable information.
items.markingKey: (a) (i) comparability [1]; (ii) faithful representation [1]; (iii) materiality [1] [3] (b) Owner's motive (e.g. higher profit/less work) [1]; benefit to users – reliable/comparable [1]; reference to concept [1] [3]

items.stem: Which concept would be abandoned if a business were about to close down?
items.answer: Going concern
items.markingKey: Going concern. Assets would be valued at break-up value [1]

items.stem: Pampas Leather values its closing inventory at its net realisable value of $26,800, which is below its cost of $37,600. A student stated that situation above is an example of the consistency concept. Identify the error and state the correct concept.
items.answer: The situation shows prudence: profits and assets should not be overstated and losses and liabilities should not be understated; consistency means once a method is chosen it should be used from year to year so that results can be compared. Correct concept: prudence.
items.markingKey: Error: the situation shows prudence: profits and assets should not be overstated and losses and liabilities should not be understated; consistency means once a method is chosen it should be used from year to year so that results can be compared [1]; correct concept: prudence [1] [2]

items.stem: The auditors of Monsoon Garments were concerned that a major customer owing $33,900 had collapsed and that the business might have to close; they questioned whether assets should be valued at break-up values. Identify the accounting concept applied.
items.answer: Going concern.
items.markingKey: going concern [1]

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) Cedar Hardware continues to value inventory using FIFO, as in previous years, so that this year's gross profit can be compared with last year's (ii) Atlas Engineering values its machinery at cost less depreciation of $36,100 rather than at the $47,900 it would fetch if sold today. Identify the accounting concept applied in each situation.
items.answer: (i) consistency; (ii) going concern
items.markingKey: (i) consistency [1]; (ii) going concern [1] [2]

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) Monsoon Garments paid insurance of $13,400 on 1 October covering twelve months; only three months' cost is charged in the year ended 31 December (ii) Jade Ceramics values its closing inventory at its net realisable value of $21,100, which is below its cost of $36,700 (iii) Pampas Leather has a highly skilled and loyal workforce, but this is not shown as an asset in its statement of financial position. (a) Identify the accounting concept applied in each situation. (b) Explain how ignoring the accruals (matching) concept would affect users of the financial statements.
items.answer: (a) (i) accruals (matching); (ii) prudence; (iii) money measurement (b) The statements would not show a true and fair view: income and expenses are recognised in the period in which they are earned or incurred, not when cash is received or paid.
items.markingKey: (a) (i) accruals (matching) [1]; (ii) prudence [1]; (iii) money measurement [1] [3] (b) Statements misleading [1]; link to concept meaning [1] [2]

items.stem: Land is shown at the price paid for it many years ago. Which concept is applied?
items.answer: Historical cost
items.markingKey: Historical cost. Assets at original cost [1]

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) A machine bought by Tundra Outdoor for $8,200 is recorded at $8,200, even though the seller's list price was higher (ii) Lotus Retail has a highly skilled and loyal workforce, but this is not shown as an asset in its statement of financial position. An accounts assistant stated that situation (i) is an example of the business entity concept. Explain why this is wrong and determine the correct concept.
items.answer: The situation shows historical cost: assets are recorded at their original cost to the business; business entity means the business is treated as separate from its owner; only business transactions are recorded. Correct concept: historical cost.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the situation shows historical cost: assets are recorded at their original cost to the business; business entity means the business is treated as separate from its owner; only business transactions are recorded [1]; working: match the situation to the definition [1]; correct concept: historical cost [1] [3]

items.stem: When Pampas Leather bought inventory on credit for $19,900, the purchases account was debited and the supplier's account credited with $19,900. Identify the accounting concept applied.
items.answer: Duality.
items.markingKey: duality [1]

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) Nile Valley Dairy has a highly skilled and loyal workforce, but this is not shown as an asset in its statement of financial position (ii) The excellent reputation of Felix for customer service is not recorded in the accounts of Pacific Tiles (iii) Pacific Tiles bought land for $21,500 ten years ago. Similar land is now worth $24,500, but the land is shown at $21,500 (iv) The auditors of Mekong Rice Mills were concerned that a major customer owing $23,100 had collapsed and that the business might have to close; they questioned whether assets should be valued at break-up values. (a) Identify the accounting concept applied in each situation. (b) Explain the money measurement concept.
items.answer: (a) (i) money measurement; (ii) money measurement; (iii) historical cost; (iv) going concern (b) Only items that can be measured in money terms are recorded.
items.markingKey: (a) (i) money measurement [1]; (ii) money measurement [1]; (iii) historical cost [1]; (iv) going concern [1] [4] (b) only items that can be measured in money terms are recorded [2]

items.stem: Harbour Electrics uses a delivery van under a five-year lease and records it as a non-current asset, although it does not legally own the van. A student stated that situation above is an example of the business entity concept. Identify the error and state the correct concept.
items.answer: The situation shows substance over form: transactions are recorded according to their economic reality rather than their legal form; business entity means the business is treated as separate from its owner; only business transactions are recorded. Correct concept: substance over form.
items.markingKey: Error: the situation shows substance over form: transactions are recorded according to their economic reality rather than their legal form; business entity means the business is treated as separate from its owner; only business transactions are recorded [1]; correct concept: substance over form [1] [2]

items.stem: Read the following situations: (i) A customer paid Pampas Leather a deposit of $19,600 in December for goods to be delivered in March; it is not included in December sales (ii) Baobab Furnishings uses a delivery van under a five-year lease and records it as a non-current asset, although it does not legally own the van (iii) The private house and car of Yusuf are not shown in the statement of financial position of Pacific Tiles. The bookkeeper stated that situation (i) is an example of the money measurement concept. Explain why this is wrong and determine the correct concept.
items.answer: The situation shows realisation: revenue is recognised when goods or services pass to the customer and the customer is liable to pay, not when cash is received; money measurement means only items that can be measured in money terms are recorded. Correct concept: realisation.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the situation shows realisation: revenue is recognised when goods or services pass to the customer and the customer is liable to pay, not when cash is received; money measurement means only items that can be measured in money terms are recorded [1]; working: match the situation to the definition [1]; correct concept: realisation [1] [3]

items.stem: A waste bin costing $19.85 that will last five years is written off as an expense by Savanna Tours in the year of purchase. Identify the accounting concept applied.
items.answer: Materiality.
items.markingKey: materiality [1]

items.stem: Lagoon Boatworks groups expenses into clear headings and explains unusual items in notes so that a non-accountant can follow its statements. The owner stated that situation above is an example of the accruals (matching) concept. State the mistake made and give the correct concept.
items.answer: The situation shows understandability: information is presented clearly so that users with reasonable knowledge can understand it; accruals (matching) means income and expenses are recognised in the period in which they are earned or incurred, not when cash is received or paid. Correct concept: understandability.
